stories.title: Texas People & Companies, October 30, 2026
stories.excerpt: Newmark arranged a bridge loan to refinance Citadel Apartments, a 293-unit Class A multifamily community located at 2220 Pinegate Drive in Houston. Newmark’s James Maynard and Robert Wright secured the financing on behalf of the borrower, Lightstone, alongside Matt Williams, Kyle Schlitt and David Williams. Greystar provided the financing through its debt fund platform. It was constructed in 2019. Pinecroft Realty completed the acquisition of Brazos Valley Medical Office Building at 3121 University Drive E in Bryan, Texas. Brazos Valley MOB is a 100% leased, two-story, 40,268-square-foot building that was developed in 2015 on a 4.76-acre site. The primary tenant of the building is Central Texas Sports Medicine. Fortec made an early education real estate acquisition, this time in the rapidly growing Austin suburb of Kyle, Texas. The Miami-based developer and investor has acquired a 17,900-square-foot preschool property on 1.95 acres, with KinderCare assuming operations under a 15-year absolute net lease. The purpose-built facility has a licensed capacity of 282 children and has operated since 2002. Lee & Associates Dallas-Fort Worth completed a new lease transaction for a 43,235-square-foot industrial space at Interstate Warehouse V at 10741-10761 King William Drive in Dallas. Adam Graham, Ken Wesson and Chris Hillman of Lee & Associates Dallas-Fort Worth represented the Landlord, EastGroup Properties. Tommy Lim of Century 21 Judge Fite Company – Frisco represented the Tenant, ULC Connects. Chris Howard has joined Kidder Mathews’ Valuation Advisory Services division as Vice President in Dallas, Texas. Howard brings more than 20 years of experience in consultative sales and business development, specializing in cost segregation, tax strategies, and client relationship management. stories.title: NCREIF Property Index Posts Ninth Consecutive Quarter of Positive Total Return
stories.excerpt: Led by seniors housing, quarterly returns rose to 1.41% in the third quarter of 2026 from 1.29% in Q2, the National Council of Real Estate Investment Fiduciaries (NCREIF) reported. The NCREIF Property Index (NPI) has now posted nine consecutive quarters of positive total return. Seniors housing returned 5.98% for the quarter, up from the 3.91% reported for Q2, with appreciation of 4.60% accounting for most of the gain and representing the index’s strongest sector result by a wide margin. Retail returned 2.04% (from 1.80%) and self-storage 1.83% (from 1.67%), both improving for a second quarter. Industrial, the largest sector at a third of the index, edged up to 1.52% from 1.49%. Office returned 1.18%, up from 0.70%, as the decline in office values slowed to 0.27% from 0.72%. The sector remains the only major property type with a negative capital return. The NPI is based on 13,200 properties, currently totaling $939 billion in market value. The post NCREIF Property Index Posts Ninth Consecutive Quarter of Positive Total Return appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: NCREIF NPI posts 1.41% Q3 return; 9 consecutive quarters positive across 13,200 properties, $939B value
Seniors housing led all sectors at 5.98% quarterly return with 4.60% appreciation; retail 2.04%, self-storage 1.83%, industrial 1.52%
Office sector remains underwater with 1.18% return and -0.27% capital depreciation; slowest decline trajectory
stories.summary: The NCREIF Property Index returned 1.41% in Q3 2026, the ninth consecutive quarter of positive total returns. Seniors housing dominated with 5.98% quarterly gains driven primarily by appreciation. Industrial, the largest sector at one-third of the index, posted 1.52% returns. Office remains the only major sector with negative capital returns at -0.27%, though depreciation is decelerating. The index represents 13,200 properties valued at $939 billion.
stories.impact: Seniors housing appreciation outpacing multifamily signals potential cap rate compression in that sector; multifamily developers should monitor if capital increasingly favors assisted living and senior communities over conventional apartments, potentially affecting financing availability and investor appetite for core-plus resi deals nationally.

stories.title: UCHealth Advancing $463M Colorado Springs Hospital Expansion
stories.excerpt: UCHealth broke ground on a $463 million expansion of UCHealth Memorial Hospital in Colorado Springs. The expansion includes more than 300,000 square feet of new construction, including a six-story inpatient tower, eight new operating rooms and an expanded emergency department with 10 new CDU units. The project will increase the hospital’s capacity from 140 to 190 beds, initially adding 34 medical-surgical beds and 14 intensive care unit beds. Approximately 45% of the new space will be built out for immediate use, while the remaining space will be shelled to accommodate future growth. The project also includes a 57,000-square-foot renovation of the existing hospital, encompassing a renovated main lobby, pharmacy and an expanded laboratory, kitchen and cafeteria. Hammes is serving as UCHealth’s owner’s representative and project manager for the major expansion. Other partners include JE Dunn as the construction manager and Perkins&Will as the architect. bullets: UCHealth breaking ground on $463M expansion of Memorial Hospital in Colorado Springs; 300K+ sq ft new construction

stories.summary: UCHealth broke ground on a $463 million expansion of UCHealth Memorial Hospital in Colorado Springs, adding over 300,000 square feet of new construction including a six-story inpatient tower with 50 new beds (140 to 190 total), eight operating rooms, and an expanded emergency department. The project also includes 57,000 square feet of renovation of existing facilities. Construction management by JE Dunn; architects Perkins&Will.
stories.impact: Major healthcare capex and permanent headcount expansion in Colorado Springs signals durable job growth and employer investment in metro; multifamily developers should view this as demand tailwind for workforce housing in Colorado Springs submarkets, particularly near medical campus; likely to attract ancillary service workers and professional tenants over 2–3 year construction window and beyond.

stories.title: Equinix Raises Outlook Again as Data Center Bookings Hit Record in Q3
stories.excerpt: Equinix raised its 2026 outlook for the third straight quarter after reporting record data center bookings as demand for artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure continues to skyrocket. The Redwood City, Calif.-based data center real estate investment trust recorded $533 million in annualized gross bookings during the third quarter, up 35 percent from a year earlier and 26 percent from the previous quarter. Pricing on new deals increased 12 percent from last year. CEO Adaire Fox-Martin told investors Wednesday that the company expects pricing power to strengthen as demand outpaces available space. “There isn’t enough capacity to satisfy the demand that we see in the market,” Fox-Martin said during the earnings call. “So we believe that we are at the very early stage of durable pricing strength going forward.” Equinix generated $2.57 billion in third-quarter revenue, down slightly from $2.63 billion in the second quarter but up 11 percent from a year earlier. Net income reached $489 million, compared with $477 million in the second quarter and $374 million in the same period last year. Funds from operations increased to $858 million, up from $854 million in the previous quarter and $707 million a year earlier. Equinix raised its 2026 total revenue forecast to between $10.33 billion and $10.37 billion, up from $10.21 billion to $10.29 billion predicted earlier. The company is also accelerating development plans. Equinix now expects to deliver nearly 40 percent more retail cabinets — which house customers’ computing and networking equipment — than initially planned for 2026. A company record of more than 13,000 cabinets are expected to become available during the fourth quarter. More than 20 percent of that capacity has already been pre-sold, while approximately 15 percent of capacity scheduled for delivery in 2027 is committed. Fox-Martin acknowledged that power constraints, regulation and community opposition have delayed some projects
bullets: Equinix Q3 annualized data center bookings hit $533M, up 35% YoY and 26% QoQ; pricing up 12% YoY
CEO cites capacity shortage; company raised full-year outlook for third consecutive quarter on AI/cloud demand tailwinds

stories.summary: Equinix reported record Q3 2026 data center bookings of $533 million annualized, up 35 percent year-over-year and 26 percent sequentially, with new deal pricing up 12 percent. CEO Adaire Fox-Martin told investors demand for AI and cloud infrastructure is outpacing available capacity, positioning the company for sustained pricing power. Equinix raised its 2026 outlook for the third straight quarter; Q3 revenue reached $2.57 billion, up 11 percent annually.
stories.impact: Data center capacity constraints and pricing strength signal continued tech/AI infrastructure investment concentration in Equinix metro footprint (Northern California Bay Area, Virginia/Northern Virginia, Texas, and other Tier-1 metros); multifamily developers in these markets should anticipate downstream tech worker hiring waves and elevated rents in 12–24 month window, particularly in submarkets proximate to data center campuses and fiber-rich corridors.

stories.title: University of Idaho Opens 451-Bed Student Housing Property
stories.excerpt: Gilbane and Rocky Mountain Companies, along with University of Idaho, celebrated the ribbon cutting of Vandal Village, a graduate and family housing complex on U of I’s Moscow campus. Located at 1010 Deakin Ave, the 200,000-square-foot complex encompasses 240 units, offering two- to four-bedroom plans. Designed to meet a range of housing needs, the development encompasses 451 total beds, including 232 for graduate students and 219 for married and parenting students. The initiative is part of a $135 million renovation and redevelopment of South Hill and Elmwood Apartments, the Wallace Residence Center and the Theophilus Residence Building. Joining Jeffrey Resetco, Senior Development Director at Gilbane, and Scott Green, President at University of Idaho, at the ribbon cutting ceremony were Blaine Eckles, Vice Provost and Dean of Student Affairs at University of Idaho, and Abagail Ikari, student at University of Idaho. The project team included Gilbane Development and Rocky Mountain Companies as the master developer team, Lydig as the contractor and Integrus and Design Collective as architects. bullets: University of Idaho opens Vandal Village, 240-unit graduate/family housing; 451 total beds, 200K sq ft complex in Moscow

stories.summary: Gilbane and Rocky Mountain Companies completed Vandal Village, a 240-unit graduate and family housing complex on the University of Idaho campus in Moscow, with 451 total beds across two- to four-bedroom units. The 200,000-square-foot development is part of a larger $135 million South Hill and Elmwood Apartments renovation and redevelopment initiative. The project was designed to serve graduate students, married students, and parenting families on campus.
stories.impact: Institutional housing (university-affiliated) in secondary markets like Moscow, Idaho signals education sector capital deployment but is unlikely to compete for private multifamily capital in growth metros; minimal impact on core development strategy for major markets, though demonstrates student housing and family housing niches remain viable for mission-driven and institutional sponsors.

stories.title: LIHI Opens 90-Unit Tiny House Village in South Park
stories.excerpt: The Low Income Housing Institute (LIHI) has opened a 90-unit tiny house village in Seattle’s South Park neighborhood. Cloverleaf Tiny House Village at 9128 10th Ave. S. is LIHI’s largest village and will operate as a 24-hour shelter, reported the Puget Sound Business Journal. The Seattle-based nonprofit developed the project in partnership with New Direction Missionary Baptist Church. Construction costs were expected to be $2.4 million ,and the 1.4-acre site is owned by an entity linked to Mac’s Upholstery. The project received nearly $2.8 million in grants from the Shelter Accelerator Fund, a public-private initiative between the city of Seattle and Challenge Seattle. Seattle Foundation contributed to the effort with funds from Microsoft, T-Mobile, Starbucks, and Seattle Mariners majority owner John Stanton and his wife, Terry Gillespie. LIHI operates tiny house villages and affordable apartments across the region, with a portfolio of more than 4,000 affordable apartments. The organization operates 19 tiny house villages in King and Pierce counties. The post LIHI Opens 90-Unit Tiny House Village in South Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: LIHI opens 90-unit tiny house village in Seattle South Park; largest LIHI village to date, 24-hour enhanced shelter model

stories.summary: The Low Income Housing Institute (LIHI) opened Cloverleaf Tiny House Village, a 90-unit tiny house complex in Seattle's South Park neighborhood, marking LIHI's largest village. Operating as a 24-hour enhanced shelter, the 1.4-acre site cost $2.4 million to construct and received $2.8 million in grants from the Shelter Accelerator Fund and contributions from Seattle Foundation, Microsoft, T-Mobile, Starbucks, and Seattle Mariners ownership. LIHI now operates 4,000+ affordable apartments and 19 tiny house villages across the region.
stories.impact: Public and philanthropic capital concentration on supportive housing and shelter alternatives in Seattle signals limited Private market multifamily supply constraints in King County; however, tiny house villages typically serve chronically unhoused and extremely low-income populations, not competing directly with market-rate apartment demand; minimal pressure on private developer returns, though demonstrates Seattle's embrace of alternative housing typologies that may shape zoning/land use policy affecting conventional multifamily projects.

stories.title: Vici Properties Q3 Earnings Hampered by Market Headwinds, Caesars Lease Unknowns
stories.excerpt: Vici Properties’ third-quarter share price performance was hit hard amid escalating capital costs facing net-lease real estate investment trusts (REITs) and uncertainty facing a regional master lease agreement with Caesars Entertainment. The REIT, which is focused heavily on casino and entertainment properties, reported that third-quarter funds from operations (FFO) attributable to common stockholders decreased 55.1 percent to $342 million compared to $762 million, or 71 cents per share, netted in the the year-ago period. The earnings were announced Thursday on the heels of Vici facing leasing unknowns as Fertitta Entertainment seeks to acquire its largest tenant, Caesars, which the firm has a regional master lease agreement with in Las Vegas. Vici recorded $458 million of current expected credit losses for the quarter, with $331 million tied to the Caesars lease agreement, which runs through 2055. “The Vici team is analyzing every dollar of our Vici income stream within our Caesars regional lease properties through various valuation prisms,” Edward Pitoniak, CEO of Vici, said during a third-quarter earnings call. “We are asking in relation to this asset-based income stream what income structuring model and potential related actions produce the greatest aggregate value for our stockholders.” Pitoniak said other factors that led to its disappointing third-quarter stockholder results were “general recent negativity” surrounding net-lease REIT stocks due to elevated interest rates, and high consumer exposure hampered by less discretionary consumer spending amid high inflation. To protect shareholders in periods of higher costs of capital, he said Vici aims to maintain its target leverage of 5.5 times earnings before interest, taxes and amortization. bullets: Vici Properties FFO plummets 55.1% YoY to $342M (Q3 2026); impacted by rising capital costs for net-lease REITs and Caesars lease uncertainty

stories.summary: Vici Properties reported a steep 55.1 percent year-over-year decline in FFO to $342 million in Q3 2026, citing escalating capital costs facing net-lease REITs and mounting uncertainty surrounding its regional master lease agreement with Caesars Entertainment in Las Vegas. The company recorded $458 million in current expected credit losses, with $331 million attributable to the Caesars lease (which runs through 2055) as Fertitta Entertainment seeks to acquire the casino operator. Vici's earnings pressure reflects broader REIT financing strain and tenant credit stress.
stories.impact: REIT capital markets stress and rising financing costs for net-lease operators signals tightened capital availability across CRE; hospitality and entertainment sector leasing turbulence (Caesars/Fertitta deal risk) poses refinancing risk for leveraged entertainment-linked tenants; multifamily developers relying on REIT equity partnerships, mezzanine financing, or hospitality-anchored mixed-use deals should anticipate higher cost of capital, longer underwriting timelines, and reduced REIT appetite for non-core or secondary-market deals in near term.

stories.title: Turner School Renews 8K-SF Lease at Feil’s 145 West 30th Street
stories.excerpt: Turner School, a continuing education provider specializing in commercial and industrial building operations and management, has renewed its 8,300-square-foot lease at the Feil Organization’s 145 West 30th Street in Midtown South, according to the landlord. This is a “long-term lease” with an asking rent of $55 per square foot, a Feil spokesperson told Commercial Observer. Turner has been a tenant at the 12-story, loft-style commercial office building in Midtown Manhattan since 2008. The school will continue to occupy the entire sixth floor of the property. “We’re excited to continue our relationship with the Feil Organization at 145 West 30th Street,” Thomas Carney, chief operating officer at Turner School, said in a statement. “Our full-floor space and central location allow us to continue serving our students and supporting our programs.” Founded in 1945, Turner School offers training in courses such as industrial refrigeration and air conditioning, according to its website. Courses can help students earn licenses leading to careers as watch engineers or property managers. The Feil Organization was represented in-house by Andrew Wiener, while Turner School was represented by Jordan Weiss from Savills. Weiss did not immediately respond to CO’s request for comment. “Turner School’s decision to renew early reflects the continued appeal of 145 West 30th Street and the value that full-floor spaces can provide to our tenants,” Wiener said in a statement. “Our ability to structure the renewal around Turner School’s needs gives them the flexibility to make their own improvements while remaining in a space that has supported their operations for years.” 145 West 30th Street is near the Penn Plaza commercial district, just south of Madison Square Garden and Pennsylvania Station. The building is home to Wave Sports & Entertainment, the Department of Motor Vehicles License Express, and nonprofit organization the InterAgency Council of Developmental Disabilities Agencies.
bullets: Turner School renews 8,300 sq ft office lease at Feil's 145 West 30th Street, Midtown South Manhattan; long-term deal at $55/SF

stories.summary: Turner School, a continuing education provider specializing in commercial building operations, renewed its 8,300-square-foot full-floor lease on the sixth floor of the Feil Organization's 145 West 30th Street in Midtown South Manhattan. The long-term lease is priced at $55 per square foot. Turner has been a tenant at the 12-story, loft-style office building since 2008.
stories.impact: Single office lease renewal in Midtown South signals limited data point on Manhattan office market; does not materially impact multifamily development strategy or apartment demand in NYC. Minimal relevance to residential sector.

stories.title: Bank OZK Leads $135M Financing for Yonkers Apartments Build
stories.excerpt: Saber-Hightower has sealed a $135 million financing package to develop a luxury apartment project in Yonkers, N.Y., Commercial Observer has learned. Bank OZK supplied a $92 million construction loan while Eagle Realty Group provided $43 million of limited partner equity for the sponsorship’s planned 282-unit the Ibex at Ridge Hill multifamily community within the Ridge Hill mixed-use center. Saber-Hightower commenced construction on the 17-story building it is developing in partnership with Rafferty Real Estate and Eagle Realty this month, with completion slated for 2028, CoStar previously reported. “This is an important milestone for our development team and for our vision of creating a best-in-class residential community at Ridge Hill,” Marty Berger, managing principal and co-founder of Saber-Hightower, said in a statement. JLL negotiated the financing with a capital markets team led by Evan Pariser, Aaron Niedermayer and John Lowe. Located at 1 Ridge Hill Boulevard 20 miles north of Midtown Manhattan, the Ibex at Ridge Hill will consist of 254 market-rate apartments with 28 units designated as affordable. The property, which is adjacent to a Whole Foods Market, will have 423 resident parking spaces. “Equity capital remains highly selective, particularly for ground-up development, so investors are looking closely at basis, location, product, sponsorship and their ability to execute,” Pariser said in a statement. “The Ibex checked those boxes, and we were able to structure a capital stack that positions the project well as it moves into construction.” Community amenities at the Ibex will include a fitness center, a swimming pool, a yoga studio, coworking space and a rooftop deck. The project was designed by Beyer Blinder Belle and ESG | Architecture & Design with Callahan Construction Managers serving as construction manager. Bank OZK did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Bank OZK closes $135M construction financing for Ibex at Ridge Hill, Yonkers; $92M construction loan + $43M LP equity
282-unit luxury apartment project by Saber-Hightower, Rafferty RE, Eagle Realty; 17-story building at Ridge Hill mixed-use; completion 2028
Active construction commenced October 2026; underwriter: Bank OZK; signals regional multifamily lending traction in Westchester County
stories.summary: Saber-Hightower secured a $135 million financing package for the Ibex at Ridge Hill, a 282-unit luxury apartment development in Yonkers, New York. Bank OZK led with a $92 million construction loan while Eagle Realty Group provided $43 million in limited partner equity. The 17-story project broke ground in October 2026 with completion targeted for 2028 within the Ridge Hill mixed-use center, located 20 miles north of Midtown Manhattan. JLL negotiated the financing.
stories.impact: Bank OZK construction financing activity and active multifamily starts in Yonkers/Ridge Hill (Westchester County) signal lender confidence in suburban NYC housing demand and strong regional fundamentals; Yonkers close proximity to Manhattan (20 miles) and Ridge Hill's mixed-use positioning attract workforce housing demand; indicates capital availability for luxury-positioned suburban multifamily and suggests valuation/pricing strength in Ring 1 and Ring 2 suburbs of NYC metro ahead of 2028 delivery.

stories.title: Newmark Revenue Up 12.7% Annually in Q3 Despite Capital Markets Slump
stories.excerpt: Newmark is anticipating big profits over the next few years and expects to reach $2 billion in annual revenue by 2029, according to the firm’s Thursday morning earnings call. The brokerage services firm said that it had seen double-digit growth on a year-over-year basis in the third quarter of 2026, which puts it on track for its best full-year performance in its history. CEO Barry Gosin is also leaving his role on a high note. Gosin announced in August he would transition from CEO to chairman of Newmark & Company Real Estate, its operating company, after 47 years. “We remain confident that our investment in resilient service lines, ongoing international expansion, the strength of the company’s brand and the continuing collaboration between our industry leading professionals will together drive Newmark’s long-term growth,” Gosin said during the earnings call. Gosin said he and his team are conducting both an internal and external search for a new CEO. Newmark’s total revenue was $973.2 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $863.5 in the same period last year, representing a 12.7 percent increase. The largest portion of the firm’s third-quarter revenue — $376 million — came from management services. Total expenses grew from the third quarter of 2025 to $889.2 million in the last three months ending Sept. 30, up from $820 million in the same period last year. Leasing increased by 26.5 percent year-over-year thanks to demand from companies linked to artificial intelligence, data centers and other technology sectors, with revenue from deal signings totaling $308.6 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $244 million in the third quarter of 2025. Capital markets were the only segment of Newmark’s balance sheet not seeing any growth, with $288.2 million in revenue compared to $301.3 million in the same three-month period a year ago. The brokerage services company targets $2 billion in annual revenue by 2029, fueled by resilient service lines and international expansion. CEO Barry Gosin announced his transition to chairman after 47 years, with an internal and external search underway for a successor. The firm demonstrated double-digit growth despite broader capital markets headwinds.
stories.impact: Newmark's revenue growth and profitability resilience despite 'capital markets slump' suggests deal volume and brokerage activity remain robust in multifamily leasing and sales even as financing tightens; expansion of service lines and international footprint may indicate multifamily developers have access to advisory and transaction capacity; however, commentary lacks detail on multifamily-specific activity—monitor Newmark earnings for residential sector detail to assess if apartment brokerage/capital markets strength is sustaining or if growth concentrated in other property types (industrial, logistics, office stabilization).
